record.name: Choose a DNA language model for genomic element annotation
record.description: Which DNA language model, and which way of using it, classifies genomic elements such as promoters, enhancers, splice sites and histone marks most accurately for my sequences?

attributes.question: Which DNA language model, and which way of using it, classifies genomic elements such as promoters, enhancers, splice sites and histone marks most accurately for my sequences?
intended_users: Researchers choosing a DNA sequence model to annotate or classify regions of a genome
Method developers comparing a new DNA language model with published ones
attributes.decision: Choose a DNA language model, and whether to probe its frozen embeddings or fine-tune it, for a sequence annotation task.
inputs: DNA sequences of the element type of interest, with genome build and species
Labelled examples, or none if only a frozen probe is planned
A compute budget, which decides whether fine-tuning is possible
attributes.output: Per-task scores for each model under each training regime, with the task's split, kept separate by benchmark.
attributes.setting: Research genome annotation from sequence. Short-range and long-range tasks, frozen probes and fine-tuning are separate comparisons; a rank on one does not transfer to another.
exclusions: Variant effect prediction, which has its own use cases for missense, regulatory, rare-disease and splicing variants
Sequence conservation scores and synthetic promoter expression level, which are not element annotation
Pooling scores across benchmarks: each runs its own models, splits and probes
Gene expression level, three-dimensional genome structure, and classifying a sequence's species or viral lineage, which answer other questions
attributes.clinical_scope: Research only. Nothing recorded here supports a clinical or diagnostic decision.
evidence_gaps: The linked evidence rests on five studies: GenBench, the GENEB leaderboard, SegmentNT, the Nucleotide Transformer benchmark and GUANinE v1.1. The models they cover overlap only partly, so a model ranked well in one may be absent from the others.
BEND, DART-Eval, GUE, Genomic Benchmarks and Gene-MTEB results are in the store on task records with no protocol, so they cannot carry a judgement yet.
GENEB is recorded as two benchmark records, the leaderboard and GENEB, which are probably one benchmark.
No conventional baseline, such as a k-mer or position-weight-matrix classifier, is recorded as the reference these models must beat.
Automated source review only. No human scientific review, and nothing here was reproduced.

record.name: Integrate single-cell datasets and correct batch effects
record.description: Which method combines single-cell datasets from different batches, laboratories or technologies while keeping the biological differences between cells?

attributes.question: Which method combines single-cell datasets from different batches, laboratories or technologies while keeping the biological differences between cells?
intended_users: Single-cell analysts combining datasets into one atlas or reference
Method developers comparing integration methods or pretrained embeddings
attributes.decision: Choose an integration method or a pretrained embedding for combining single-cell datasets.
inputs: Count matrices from several batches, with batch labels and cell-type labels where known
Whether an embedding may be trained on the data or must stay frozen
attributes.output: Batch-correction and biological-conservation scores for each method on the same datasets, and the trade-off between the two.
attributes.setting: Research single-cell analysis. Batch removal and conservation of biology pull against each other, so they are reported separately and never summed into one verdict without saying how.
exclusions: Transferring cell-type labels to a new dataset, which has its own use case
Clustering agreement or embedding separation presented as correct cell identity
attributes.clinical_scope: Research only. Nothing recorded here supports a clinical or diagnostic decision.
evidence_gaps: The linked evidence rests on two studies: the HyCell technical report, which scores frozen embeddings of eleven pretrained models and PCA on seven held-out atlases, and Kedzierska et al. 2025, which scores zero-shot embeddings of single-cell foundation models with scIB metrics. Both evaluate frozen embeddings, not integration methods run on the data.

scIB's own published results are in the store, but each result's scoring conditions carry the method configuration, so no two methods ever fall in one comparison group, and its protocol record is not reviewed.
SCMBench's RNA-ATAC integration and the Open Problems integration tasks are unreviewed or on task records, so they are not linked.
No method here has been run by Rewire. Automated source review only.
